questions.question: [Test 54 - Q1] In Lev Vygotsky's Socio-Cultural Theory, the term 'Scaffolding' refers to:
options: Temporary support given by a More Knowledgeable Other (MKO) during the learning process
Permanent structural changes in cognitive architecture
Rote memorization techniques for complex concepts
Standardized testing procedures in formative assessment
questions.explanation: Scaffolding is a supportive framework provided by a teacher or peer (MKO) within the Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD) that is gradually removed as the learner gains independence. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q2] Under the Right to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act 2009, what is the mandatory Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) prescribed for primary schools (Classes I to V)?
questions.explanation: As per the RTE Act 2009, the Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) for primary schools (Classes 1-5) is mandated at 30:1 for enrollment up to 200 students. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q3] Formative Assessment is primarily aimed at which of the following instructional goals?
options: Providing ongoing feedback to improve learning and teaching during the instructional process
Assigning final grades at the end of an academic semester
Certifying students for university admission
Ranking students based on normative curve distribution
questions.explanation: Formative assessment is 'Assessment FOR Learning' designed to monitor student learning and provide continuous feedback to teachers and students to modify teaching-learning activities. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q4] In Bloom's Revised Taxonomy (Anderson & Krathwohl, 2001), which level represents the highest order of cognitive processing?
options: Creating
Evaluating
Analyzing
Applying
questions.explanation: In Anderson & Krathwohl's revised taxonomy (2001), 'Creating' (generating new ideas or products) replaced 'Evaluation' at the highest cognitive level. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q5] Which teaching model is based on Jerome Bruner's concept of Discovery Learning and Enactive-Iconic-Symbolic modes of representation?
options: Constructivist Learning Model
Direct Instruction Model
Behaviorist Conditioning Model
Grammar-Translation Model
questions.explanation: Bruner proposed constructivist discovery learning where learners build knowledge through enactive (action-based), iconic (image-based), and symbolic (language-based) modes. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q6] Inclusive Education in Indian classrooms fundamentally implies:
options: Educating children with special needs alongside non-disabled children in regular classrooms with appropriate adaptations
Establishing separate special schools for children with disabilities
Admitting only high-achieving gifted students in mainstream schools
Providing home-based schooling for all children with mild learning difficulties
questions.explanation: Inclusive education ensures that all children, regardless of their physical, cognitive, social, or linguistic abilities, learn together in the same mainstream educational environment. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q7] In Howard Gardner's Theory of Multiple Intelligences, a person with high ability to perceive and understand others' moods, motivations, and feelings possesses high:
options: Interpersonal Intelligence
Intrapersonal Intelligence
Spatial Intelligence
Bodily-Kinesthetic Intelligence
questions.explanation: Interpersonal intelligence involves understanding and interacting effectively with others, whereas Intrapersonal intelligence involves self-awareness and self-understanding. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q8] What is the primary objective of Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation (CCE)?
options: To evaluate all aspects of student development, including scholastic and co-scholastic domains continuously
To conduct quarterly written examinations to eliminate low performers
To substitute internal assessments with final external board examinations
To reduce teacher workload by automating grading systems
questions.explanation: CCE evaluates both scholastic (academic) and co-scholastic (life skills, attitudes, values) growth of a learner continuously throughout the academic cycle. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q9] According to Lawrence Kohlberg's theory of Moral Development, an individual who obeys rules solely to avoid punishment is at which stage?
options: Pre-conventional Level (Stage 1: Punishment and Obedience Orientation)
Conventional Level (Stage 3: Good Boy-Nice Girl Orientation)
Post-conventional Level (Stage 5: Social Contract Orientation)
Conventional Level (Stage 4: Law and Order Orientation)
questions.explanation: Stage 1 of Kohlberg's Pre-conventional level is characterized by obedience driven by fear of physical punishment or deference to superior power. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q10] Which of the following best describes the concept of 'Diagnostic Teaching' in pedagogy?
options: Identifying specific learning difficulties and gaps in students to plan targeted remedial instruction
Conducting annual medical checkups for students in government schools
Sorting students into homogenous sections based on IQ scores
Delivering lectures without asking questions to test retention
questions.explanation: Diagnostic assessment identifies specific areas of weakness or misconceptions, serving as the basis for remedial teaching strategies. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q11] In Carl Rogers' Humanistic Theory of Education, the role of the teacher is primarily envisioned as a:
options: Facilitator of experiential learning
Strict disciplinarian and authority figure
Passive observer without instructional intervention
Direct transmitter of factual information
questions.explanation: Rogers emphasized person-centered education where the teacher acts as a facilitator providing an empathetic, authentic, and accepting environment for self-directed learning. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q12] Which of the following is an example of an 'Intrinsic Motivation' factor in student learning?
options: Inherent curiosity and personal satisfaction derived from mastering a subject
Receiving cash prizes and gold medals from the school principal
Avoidance of parental disapproval or detention after school
Desire to secure first position in class merit list
questions.explanation: Intrinsic motivation arises from internal rewards—such as curiosity, interest, personal enjoyment, or autonomy—rather than external incentives or punishments. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q13] Action Research in classroom pedagogy is defined as:
options: A reflective process conducted by teachers to solve immediate practical problems in their own classroom
Pure theoretical research conducted by university professors
Nationwide statistical survey on school enrollment ratios
Historical analysis of ancient educational systems
questions.explanation: Action research is practitioner-based inquiry aimed at diagnosing and solving specific classroom problems to enhance pedagogical effectiveness. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q14] Which learning disability specifically affects mathematical calculations, numerical reasoning, and understanding of arithmetic concepts?
options: Dyscalculia
Dyslexia
Dysgraphia
Dyspraxia
questions.explanation: Dyscalculia is a specific learning disorder that impairs an individual's ability to learn, understand, and perform mathematical operations and number relationships. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q15] The term 'Hidden Curriculum' in educational sociology refers to:
options: Unwritten, unofficial, and unintended lessons, values, and perspectives that students learn in school
Secret syllabi taught only to select advanced students
Topics deleted from the official textbook by the examination board
Extracurricular sports activities held outside school hours
questions.explanation: The hidden curriculum consists of unspoken social norms, values, behaviors, and cultural expectations transmitted implicitly through the school environment. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q16] In Micro-Teaching, what is the standard ideal duration for a single micro-teaching cycle (Teach -> Feedback -> Re-plan -> Re-teach -> Re-feedback)?
options: 36 Minutes
45 Minutes
20 Minutes
60 Minutes
questions.explanation: The standard NCERT micro-teaching cycle duration is 36 minutes: Teach (6m), Feedback (6m), Re-plan (12m), Re-teach (6m), Re-feedback (6m). (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q17] According to B.F. Skinner's Operant Conditioning, 'Positive Reinforcement' involves:
options: Presenting a rewarding stimulus following a desired behavior to increase its frequency
Removing an unpleasant stimulus to reduce unwanted behavior
Administering a painful stimulus to suppress a bad habit
Ignoring the behavior until it naturally extinguishes
questions.explanation: Positive reinforcement strengthens a behavior by providing a pleasant or desirable consequence immediately following that behavior. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q18] National Curriculum Framework (NCF) 2005 emphasizes connecting knowledge to life outside the school and ensuring that learning shifts away from:
options: Rote methods of learning
Conceptual understanding
Critical thinking skills
Constructivist inquiry
questions.explanation: NCF 2005 guiding principles mandate shifting learning away from rote memorization towards meaningful, context-based conceptual understanding. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q19] In Ivan Pavlov's classical conditioning paradigm, the buzzer or bell before conditioning is established represents the:
options: Neutral Stimulus
Unconditioned Stimulus
Conditioned Response
Unconditioned Response
questions.explanation: Before conditioning, the bell is a neutral stimulus because it does not naturally elicit the target response (salivation) until paired with food. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).

questions.question: [Test 54 - Q20] Albert Bandura's Social Learning Theory emphasizes that children learn complex social behaviors primarily through:
options: Observation, imitation, and modeling
Trial and error with explicit rewards
Rote memorization and recitation
Biological maturation and sensory reflexes
questions.explanation: Bandura's key contribution is that learning occurs through observing, imitating, and modeling the behaviors, attitudes, and emotional reactions of others. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 54).
